questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Python runs only the FIRST block whose condition is true. 15 > 10, so it prints 'big' and skips the rest, even though 15 > 5 is also true.

questions.question: What's the difference between `=` and `==`?
options: = assigns a value; == compares two values
questions.explanation: x = 5 points x at 5. x == 5 asks 'is x equal to 5?' and gives True or False.

questions.question: When is `age >= 18 and has_ticket` True?
options: When at least one part is True
Only when both parts are True
Only when both parts are False
questions.explanation: 'and' needs both sides to be True. 'or' needs at least one.

questions.question: Which value counts as False in an `if`?
questions.explanation: Empty values ("", [], {}, 0, None) are 'falsy'. "False" and [0] aren't empty, and -1 isn't zero, so they all count as True.
